clue.text: Latin lover?

parts.note: not a smouldering romantic but a scholar who loves the Latin language and ancient literature

explanation.surface: A suave Mediterranean romancer is suggested.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Latin lover' is the stock phrase for a passionate southern European charmer; the question mark invites a literal reading: someone who loves Latin.
explanation.definitionFit: A scholar of Greek and Roman antiquity is by trade devoted to the Latin tongue.

clue.text: For example, this board game's no party

indicators.note: the board game is left with no party, so those letters are taken away

parts.note: Cluedo is the British name of the murder-mystery board game
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A board game is said to be no fun at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: CLUEDO is the UK name for the board game known as Clue in America. 'For example, this' is the definition: the clue you are reading is an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Each line of a crossword is one of these hints, so the clue in front of you is an example.

clue.text: Venerable Scots archbishop keeping his head well down

indicators.note: the archbishop's first letter is moved further down the word

parts.note: William Laud was Archbishop of Canterbury under Charles I

explanation.surface: A Scottish churchman lies low.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeping his head well down' sends the L of LAUD down to the end, giving AULD.
explanation.definitionFit: Auld is the Scots form of old, as in Auld Lang Syne, so it means aged or venerable.

clue.text: Is partisan group after a day for reparation?

indicators.note: the words before it are placed following the day

parts.note: Sat is the abbreviation for Saturday
a faction is a dissenting group within a larger body

explanation.surface: A political group asking for compensation for a past day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is' is used as plain letters, though it reads as the verb; 'a day' is the standard abbreviation for Saturday.
explanation.definitionFit: Satisfaction in its older sense is atonement or amends made for a wrong.

clue.text: Put caught fish right inside here?

definitions.text: Put caught fish right inside here?

indicators.note: the abbreviation for right is put within the other letters

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
the eel is a snakelike fish

explanation.surface: An angler is told where to put the fish just landed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' places R within C plus EEL. The whole clue also defines: an angler's basket, where a caught fish goes.
explanation.definitionFit: A creel is a wicker basket in which anglers keep their catch.

clue.text: Laborious task to deal with — changing fillings for fancy cake?

indicators.note: the middles of the two words are swapped with each other

parts.note: a sweat is a hard grind

indicators.note: the inner letters of each word are the parts exchanged

parts.note: to meet a problem is to deal with it

explanation.surface: A tedious chore is rescued by new fillings for a fancy cake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing fillings' swaps the middles: SWEAT gives up EA for the EE of MEET, which takes EA in return, making SWEET and MEAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweetmeat is an old word for a sweet delicacy such as a candied fruit or small cake.

clue.text: Cut free

definitions.meaning: slang sense of spare, surplus, going for nothing

explanation.definitionFit: Gash is both a deep cut and, in service slang, something spare and available for nothing.

clue.text: Early Victorian? Much earlier than that!

definitions.text: Early Victorian? Much earlier than that!

parts.words: Early Victorian? Much earlier than that!
parts.note: Victorian means from the Australian state of Victoria, and the earliest inhabitants there long predate the nineteenth century

explanation.surface: A remark on someone from the 1840s who seems even older.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Victorian' suggests the reign of Queen Victoria; it means from Victoria in Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: Aboriginal Australians are the original peoples, there tens of thousands of years before settlers.

clue.text: One whose staff are often in a class of their own

definitions.text: One whose staff are often in a class of their own

parts.words: One whose staff are often in a class of their own
parts.note: the head of a school, whose teaching staff each take a class

explanation.surface: Praise for someone with an exceptional team of employees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a class of their own' sounds like praise; here the teachers literally each have their own class.
explanation.definitionFit: The man in charge of a school employs the teachers, each running a classroom.

clue.text: Not well educated? So your grid is empty

definitions.meaning: a crossword grid with no letters written in it yet

explanation.definitionFit: Lacking schooling means illiterate, and a blank grid literally has no letters entered.

clue.text: Fish with a tail

parts.note: the cod is a common food fish

explanation.surface: A fish is described by its tail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tail' is the definition in its musical sense: a closing passage added to a piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A coda is the concluding section tacked onto the end of a musical movement.

clue.text: Absolute Italian revolutionary — far from liberal

indicators.note: turning over, so the letters of the word are overturned into a new order

parts.note: the word Italian is the fodder as printed; the setter needed an R where its L stands, so the corrected letters are shown
total means complete or absolute

explanation.surface: An out-and-out Italian rebel who is anything but liberal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revolutionary' rearranges the fodder, but ITALIAN has an L where the answer needs an R, so as printed the letters cannot give ITARIAN: a setter's slip.
explanation.definitionFit: A totalitarian regime allows no opposition, the opposite of a liberal one.

clue.text: Such as might make you omit liaisons?

definitions.text: Such as might make you omit liaisons?

indicators.note: the following words are the raw material out of which something else might be made, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A policy that would make you avoid alliances is described.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines: a policy of standing apart from other nations avoids liaisons, and the letters of OMIT LIAISONS rearrange to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A national policy of keeping out of alliances and foreign entanglements is a way of omitting liaisons.

clue.text: Being sick with changed order for education

indicators.note: the two parts of the phrase swap places

parts.note: bringing up food means vomiting

explanation.surface: Being ill reshuffles a child's schooling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with changed order' moves the UP of BRINGING UP to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: Upbringing is the rearing and training of a child, a form of education.

clue.text: Odd time, not totally satisfying, without much happening

parts.note: an odd number is uneven

indicators.note: the word is left incomplete, its final letter dropped

parts.note: a full meal is satisfying

explanation.surface: A strange, unfulfilling period when nothing occurred.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not totally' cuts the last L from FULL.
explanation.definitionFit: An uneventful period is quiet, with nothing notable taking place.

clue.text: Long drink containing gouged out pulp and fruit

parts.note: to long for is to pine

indicators.note: the drink holds the next piece inside it

parts.note: ale is a beer

indicators.note: the inside of the word pulp is scooped away, leaving only its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A tall glass holding a mashed fruit pulp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long drink' looks like one phrase, a tall cocktail, but splits into two separate pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The pineapple is a tropical fruit with spiky skin and sweet yellow flesh.

clue.text: Opium Anne misused for this ailment

indicators.note: abused or put to wrong use, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Anne's opium abuse has led to a disease.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misused' rearranges OPIUM and ANNE.
explanation.definitionFit: Pneumonia is an inflammation of the lungs, a serious illness.

clue.text: Revealing fault with a girl

parts.note: miss is a title for a girl or unmarried woman

explanation.surface: A fault is exposed in a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Something amiss is faulty or wrong, showing that there is a fault.

clue.text: Strive to hold this to make fast

indicators.note: the words strive to hold the answer within their letters, spanning the gap between them

explanation.surface: An effort to grip something firmly in place.
explanation.definitionFit: To rivet is to fasten parts securely together with a metal pin.

clue.text: Frantically trace exit to get out from difficult situation

indicators.note: done in a wild frenzy, so the letters of the two words are thrown about

explanation.surface: Someone desperately looks for the way out of a tight spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frantically' rearranges TRACE and EXIT together.
explanation.definitionFit: To extricate is to free or disentangle someone from a difficulty.

clue.text: Officer's given hand to man sitting on the fence

parts.note: a non-com is a non-commissioned officer, informally
mitt is slang for a hand
Al is a man's name

explanation.surface: An officer offers his hand to an indecisive fellow.
explanation.walkthrough: NONCOM is short for non-commissioned officer, such as a sergeant or corporal.
explanation.definitionFit: Refusing to take a side, as a fence-sitter does, is being uncommitted.

clue.text: Trunk and tangled roots

indicators.note: twisted and knotted, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A tree's trunk and its matted roots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trunk' suggests a tree, as do the roots; it means the human body.
explanation.definitionFit: The torso is the body's trunk, without head or limbs.

clue.text: Use padding to protect one seasonal flower

parts.note: to wad is to stuff or pad with soft material
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Wrap a seasonal bloom in padding to protect it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' is something that flows: a desert valley whose stream runs only in the rainy season.
explanation.definitionFit: A wadi is a dry riverbed in arid lands that carries water only after seasonal rains.

clue.text: Shakespearean clown's. given up second charity event

indicators.note: the clown surrenders that letter, so it is removed

parts.note: Feste is the clown in Twelfth Night

explanation.surface: A Shakespearean jester takes a moment off for a fundraiser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given up' removes S from FESTE. A fete is a British outdoor fundraising fair.
explanation.definitionFit: A fete is an outdoor fair, usually held to raise money for a good cause.

clue.text: News of Northern Ireland slipping back

indicators.note: the run of letters slides backwards, so it is read in reverse

explanation.surface: A report about Northern Ireland going downhill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is not a link here but part of the letters that are turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: Info is short for information, which is what news supplies.

clue.text: A rendition that's drunk and disorderly

indicators.note: intoxicated and reeling, so the letters stagger into a new order

explanation.surface: A drunken, rowdy performance of a song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' rearranges A RENDITION; 'disorderly' is the old sense of unregulated, beyond proper bounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Inordinate originally meant not in order, unregulated, hence excessive.

clue.text: Good beer can give you such, wind

parts.note: ale is a type of beer

explanation.surface: Drinking good beer gives you flatulence.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface jokes that beer gives you wind; the definition is a strong wind.
explanation.definitionFit: A gale is a very strong wind.

clue.text: Dressing in a mixture of greens?

definitions.text: Dressing in a mixture of greens?

parts.words: Dressing in a mixture of greens?
parts.note: the sauce that a mixed green salad might be dressed with, a creamy egg and oil emulsion

explanation.surface: A dressing tossed through a mixed leaf salad.
explanation.definitionFit: Mayonnaise is a cold dressing made from egg yolks and oil, often used on salads.
